title: Easy exam 5
about: Ten single-choice questions on the basics: one concept each, with the classic look-alike options.

questions.title: Find by size
questions.text: Which command finds the files under `/var` that are larger than 10 megabytes?

options.t: `find /var -size 10M`
options.why: Without a sign the size must be exactly 10 M (rounded up), not larger.

options.t: `find /var -size -10M`
options.why: `-` means smaller than 10 M.

options.t: `find /var -size +10M`
options.why: `+` means larger than, and the letter `M` gives the unit in megabytes.

options.t: `find /var -size +10`
options.why: Without a letter the unit is a 512-byte block, so this finds files above about 5 KB.

questions.title: Octal modes
questions.text: Which statement about `chmod 640 notes.txt` is TRUE?

options.t: The owner can only read; the group can read and write; the others can do nothing.
options.why: Digit by digit: 6 is `rw-` (owner), 4 is `r--` (group), 0 is `---` (others).

options.t: The owner and the group can read and write; the others can read.
options.why: That would be `chmod 664`.

options.t: The owner can read and write; the group can only read; the others have no permissions.
The owner can read, write and execute; the group can read; the others can do nothing.
options.why: The `x` bit has value 1; a 7 would be needed for the owner.

questions.title: Redirecting only the errors
questions.text: Which statement about `command 2> err.txt` is FALSE?

options.t: The error messages of `command` go to `err.txt` instead of the screen.
options.why: True: `2` is the file descriptor of stderr.

options.t: The normal output of `command` still appears on the screen.
options.why: True: only stderr was redirected.

options.t: If `command` prints no error, `err.txt` is left untouched.
options.why: False: `2>` creates or empties the file before the command runs, even if nothing is written to it.

options.t: `command 2>> err.txt` adds the errors at the end of the file instead of replacing it.
options.why: True: `>>` appends.

questions.title: Manual sections
questions.text: Which command shows the manual page of `printf` from section 3, the C library, instead of the shell command in section 1?

options.t: `man printf`
options.why: It shows the first page found, normally the one in section 1.

options.t: `man printf 3`
options.why: The section goes before the name; here `man` would also look for a page called `3`.

options.t: `man 3 printf`
options.why: `man section name` selects the section.

options.t: `man -3 printf`
options.why: `-3` is not an option of `man`; the section is given as a plain number.

questions.title: All the processes
questions.text: Which command lists the processes of all the users, including the user name of each one?

options.t: `ps`
options.why: By default it shows only the processes of the current terminal and user.

options.t: `ps -l`
options.why: `-l` gives a long format, but still for the processes of the current terminal.

options.t: `ps aux`
options.why: `a` shows the processes of other users, `x` also those without a terminal and `u` the user.

options.t: `ps -a`
options.why: `-a` shows the processes associated with a terminal, without the user column.

questions.title: HOME after cd
questions.text: The user `ana` runs `cd /tmp` and then `echo $HOME`. What is printed?

options.t: `/tmp`
options.why: `HOME` does not follow the current directory.
`HOME` is not the root directory.

options.t: `/home/ana`
options.why: `HOME` is the starting directory of the user and it stays the same when you change directory.

options.t: An empty line, because `HOME` is only defined in the directory where the session started.
options.why: It is a variable of the environment, defined wherever you are.

questions.title: touch and mktemp
questions.text: Which statement about `touch` and `mktemp` is FALSE?

options.t: `touch new.txt` creates an empty file if `new.txt` does not exist.
options.why: True.

options.t: `touch old.txt` on an existing file changes its modification time.
options.why: True: that is what the name suggests.

options.t: `touch old.txt` empties an existing file before updating its time.
options.why: False: `touch` never changes the content of a file.

options.t: `mktemp` creates an empty temporary file with a random name in `/tmp` and prints its name.
options.why: True: for example `/tmp/tmp.XXXXXXXXXX` with random characters.

questions.title: egrep
questions.text: What is the difference between `egrep` and `grep`?

options.t: `egrep` is `grep -E`: it reads extended regular expressions, where `+`, `?`, `|` and `( )` are special.
options.why: It is a shortcut for the option.

options.t: `egrep` also searches inside the subdirectories, which `grep` never does by itself.
options.why: That is `grep -r` (or `rgrep`).

options.t: `egrep` ignores the difference between upper and lower case, which `grep` cannot do.
options.why: That is `grep -i`.

options.t: `egrep` reads only what arrives through a pipe, while `grep` reads only from named files.
options.why: Both read the files given or, without files, the standard input.

questions.title: One word or many
questions.text: `a.sh` contains `for a in "$*"; do echo "[$a]"; done`. What does `bash a.sh "x y" z` print?

options.t: `[x y]` and `[z]` on two lines
options.why: That is what `"$@"` would give, keeping each argument.

options.t: `[x]`, `[y]` and `[z]` on three lines
options.why: That is the result of the unquoted `$*`.

options.t: `[x y z]` on one line
options.why: `"$*"` joins all the arguments in one single string, so the loop runs once.

options.t: Nothing, because `$*` only works outside a loop.
options.why: `$*` can be used anywhere in a script.

questions.title: Fields of passwd
questions.text: A line of `/etc/passwd` is `ana:x:1001:100:Ana Ruiz:/home/ana:/bin/bash`. Which statement is TRUE?

options.t: The UID is 100 and the primary GID is 1001.
options.why: The fields are in the order UID then GID.

options.t: The `x` is the password of ana in plain text.
options.why: The `x` only says that the password is stored elsewhere, in `/etc/shadow`.

options.t: Her home directory is `/bin/bash` and her shell is `/home/ana`.
options.why: The home is the sixth field and the shell the seventh.

options.t: The UID is 1001, the primary GID is 100 and the login shell is `/bin/bash`.
options.why: Third, fourth and last field.
